description: PiS leader Jaroslaw Kaczynski announced the 'Piatka Kaczynskiego' package of new social transfers (child benefit extension, extra pension payment) ahead of the 2019 elections.
US President Trump announced he would raise tariffs on 200 billion USD of Chinese goods from 10% to 25%, escalating the US-China trade war.
European Parliament election in Poland; exit poll at 21:00 showed PiS ahead of the European Coalition.
The CJEU ruled in the Dziubak case (C-260/18) that Polish courts may annul CHF-indexed mortgage contracts containing unfair terms.
Polish parliamentary election; exit poll at 21:00 showed PiS retaining a Sejm majority.
Second Morawiecki government sworn in; new Ministry of State Assets created under Jacek Sasin taking over supervision of state energy companies, and Michal Kurtyka appointed climate minister.
European Commission presented the European Green Deal with a 2050 climate-neutrality goal.
European Council endorsed EU climate neutrality by 2050 with Poland exempted from committing to implement the target at that stage.
The Sejm passed the judiciary disciplinary law (so-called 'muzzle law') criticised by the European Commission.
A US strike in Baghdad killed Iranian general Qasem Soleimani, raising US-Iran tensions.
President Andrzej Duda signed the judiciary disciplinary ('muzzle') law opposed by the European Commission.
Polish government announced closure of schools and universities due to COVID-19, followed by a state of epidemic threat.
Government presented the COVID-19 'Anti-Crisis Shield' (Tarcza Antykryzysowa) economic package.
Jaroslaw Kaczynski and Jaroslaw Gowin announced that the 10 May presidential election would not take place as planned.
Originally scheduled presidential election day; the vote was not held (postal vote cancelled).
First round of the Polish presidential election; exit poll showed Andrzej Duda first and Rafal Trzaskowski second.
Second round of the presidential election; Andrzej Duda re-elected.
Government and mining unions signed an agreement setting the end of hard-coal mining in Poland by 2049.
Government adopted the updated Polish Nuclear Power Programme planning 6-9 GW of nuclear capacity, first unit by 2033.
Government reconstruction: Jaroslaw Kaczynski joined the cabinet as deputy PM; Ministry of Climate and Environment formed under Michal Kurtyka.
US media projected Joe Biden the winner of the 2020 US presidential election.
Poland and Hungary blocked the EU 2021-2027 budget and recovery fund over the rule-of-law conditionality mechanism.
KNF chairman Jacek Jastrzebski presented to bankers a proposal of voluntary settlements converting CHF mortgages into zloty loans.
EU summit reached a compromise ending the Polish-Hungarian veto of the EU budget and recovery fund.
EU leaders agreed to raise the 2030 emissions reduction target to at least 55%.
Council of Ministers adopted Energy Policy of Poland until 2040 (PEP2040) envisaging coal phase-down and nuclear power.
Sejm ratified the EU Own Resources Decision enabling the Recovery Fund, with Left opposition support.
PiS presented the 'Polish Deal' (Polski Lad) tax and social programme.
CJEU ordered Poland to immediately halt mining at PGE's Turow lignite mine as an interim measure.
Government and mining unions signed the social contract on mining transformation (mine closures by 2049).
European Commission presented the Fit for 55 package including EU ETS reform; same day CJEU issued interim order on Polish judiciary.
CJEU ruled the Polish Supreme Court Disciplinary Chamber incompatible with EU law.
PM Morawiecki dismissed Deputy PM Jaroslaw Gowin, leading Porozumienie to leave the ruling coalition.
CJEU fined Poland 500,000 EUR per day for failing to halt mining at the Turow mine.
Constitutional Tribunal ruled (K 3/21) that some EU treaty provisions are incompatible with the Polish constitution.
Anna Moskwa appointed Minister of Climate and Environment replacing Michal Kurtyka.
CJEU fined Poland 1 million EUR per day over the Supreme Court Disciplinary Chamber.
Escalation of the Belarus-Poland border crisis as large migrant groups massed at Kuznica crossing.
President Duda signed the Polish Deal (Polski Lad) tax reform.
Energy regulator URE approved 2022 household electricity tariffs with substantial increases.
Poland and the Czech Republic signed an agreement ending the Turow mine dispute.
Finance Minister Tadeusz Koscinski resigned after the Polish Deal tax reform controversy.
Vladimir Putin recognised the separatist Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' and ordered troops into eastern Ukraine.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
Council of Ministers approved the plan to spin off coal generation assets of state utilities into NABE (National Energy Security Agency).
PM Morawiecki announced plan to end imports of Russian coal, gas and oil by end-2022.
PM Morawiecki announced a government plan to support mortgage borrowers including payment holidays (wakacje kredytowe).
Gazprom informed PGNiG it would halt gas deliveries to Poland from 27 April under the Yamal contract.
European Commission endorsed Poland's Recovery Plan (KPO) with judiciary-related milestones.
President Duda signed the law introducing mortgage payment holidays for 2022-2023.
Putin announced partial military mobilisation in Russia.
Council of Ministers adopted a draft law freezing 2023 household electricity prices at 2022 levels up to 2,000 kWh.
Explosions damaged the Nord Stream 1 and 2 gas pipelines in the Baltic Sea.
EU energy ministers agreed emergency measures including a cap on inframarginal power generators' revenues and a solidarity contribution.
Sejm gave final approval to the 2023 household electricity price freeze law.
Sejm passed the law capping electricity prices for SMEs and public entities at 785 PLN/MWh and requiring generators to pay contributions to a price-difference fund (windfall levy).
PM Morawiecki announced Westinghouse technology was selected for Poland's first nuclear power plant.
A missile fell on Przewodow in eastern Poland killing two people during a Russian strike on Ukraine.
EU Council and Parliament reached a provisional deal on EU ETS reform and creation of ETS2 under Fit for 55.
Sejm passed the Supreme Court law amendment intended to meet KPO milestones and unlock EU recovery funds.
President Duda referred the Supreme Court amendment (KPO milestone) to the Constitutional Tribunal instead of signing.
President Duda signed the law creating a commission on Russian influence ('Lex Tusk').
CJEU ruled that Poland's 2019 judiciary disciplinary ('muzzle') law violated EU law.
CJEU ruled (C-520/21) that banks cannot claim remuneration for use of capital after annulment of CHF loan contracts.
Wagner Group mutiny in Russia.
Hamas attack on Israel triggered the Israel-Hamas war.
Polish parliamentary election; exit poll showed PiS first but KO, Third Way and Left with a combined majority.
President Duda designated Mateusz Morawiecki to form a government despite lack of a majority.
Third Morawiecki government sworn in.
Sejm rejected confidence in Morawiecki's government and elected Donald Tusk as prime minister.
Tusk government sworn in; Borys Budka Minister of State Assets, Paulina Hennig-Kloska climate minister, Andrzej Domanski finance minister.
President Duda signed the law extending the household electricity price freeze into H1 2024.
Orlen supervisory board dismissed CEO Daniel Obajtek as part of management changes at state companies after the change of government.
PGE supervisory board dismissed CEO Wojciech Dabrowski and two vice-presidents.
Ursula von der Leyen announced in Warsaw the release of up to 137 billion EUR of EU funds for Poland, unblocking the KPO.
Industry Minister Marzena Czarnecka announced the government was abandoning the NABE coal-asset spin-off plan.
First round of Polish local elections.
Iran launched its first direct drone and missile attack on Israel.
Second round of local elections (mayoral run-offs).
Polish Supreme Court adopted a full-chamber resolution on CHF loan cases.
President Duda signed the amendment introducing 2024 mortgage payment holidays with an income criterion.
European Commission announced its intention to close the Article 7 rule-of-law procedure against Poland.
Jakub Jaworowski appointed Minister of State Assets replacing Borys Budka (running for European Parliament) in a cabinet reshuffle.
President Duda signed the energy voucher law setting a maximum household electricity price of 500 PLN/MWh for H2 2024.
European Parliament election in Poland; exit poll showed KO narrowly ahead of PiS.
Iran fired a large ballistic missile salvo at Israel.
Donald Trump won the US presidential election.
President Duda signed the law extending the 500 PLN/MWh household electricity price cap until end-September 2025.
Donald Trump inaugurated for his second term as US president.
Trump signed orders imposing tariffs on Canada, Mexico and China.
Oval Office confrontation between Trump and Zelensky; US later paused military aid to Ukraine.
Ursula von der Leyen presented the ReArm Europe defence plan including SAFE loans.
Trump announced 'Liberation Day' reciprocal tariffs, including 20% on the EU.
Trump announced a 90-day pause of most reciprocal tariffs.
President Duda signed the law keeping the household electricity price cap of 500 PLN/MWh until end-September 2025.
First round of the Polish presidential election; exit poll showed Rafal Trzaskowski narrowly ahead of Karol Nawrocki.
Second round of the presidential election; exit poll showed a near tie and final results (2 June) gave victory to Karol Nawrocki.
Tusk government won a vote of confidence in the Sejm after the presidential election defeat.
Israel launched large-scale strikes on Iran, starting the Twelve-Day War.
The United States struck Iranian nuclear sites at Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan.
Trump announced an Israel-Iran ceasefire.
Trump announced a 30% tariff on EU imports from 1 August.
Tusk announced government reconstruction: Ministry of Energy restored under Milosz Motyka, Wojciech Balczun State Assets minister, Andrzej Domanski finance and economy superminister.
US and EU announced a trade framework deal with a 15% US tariff on most EU goods.
Karol Nawrocki sworn in as President of Poland.
Trump-Putin summit in Alaska on the war in Ukraine.
President Nawrocki vetoed the wind-farm siting law that also contained the Q4 2025 household electricity price freeze.
Ministry of Finance published plan to raise CIT for banks to 30% in 2026 (declining later) and change the bank tax.
President Nawrocki vetoed the energy deregulation act (renewable concession thresholds) and other laws.
Russian drones violated Polish airspace overnight and were shot down; Poland invoked NATO Article 4.
President Nawrocki signed the law extending the 500 PLN/MWh household electricity price freeze to end-2025.
PM Tusk confirmed sabotage (explosion) on the Warsaw-Lublin railway line, attributed to Russian services.
President Nawrocki signed the law raising CIT for banks from 2026 and amending the bank tax.
European Commission approved state aid for Poland's first nuclear power plant.
EU negotiators agreed the 2040 climate target (90%) and a one-year delay of ETS2 to 2028.
Energy Minister Motyka stated the government does not foresee freezing electricity prices in 2026.
URE approved 2026 household electricity tariffs averaging 495.16 PLN/MWh net, below the expiring freeze level.
CJEU ruled that the Polish Constitutional Tribunal violated EU law and is not an independent court.
PM Tusk confirmed late-December 2025 cyberattacks on wind farms and two CHP plants, likely Russian sabotage.
Katarzyna Pelczynska-Nalecz elected leader of coalition party Polska 2050, replacing Szymon Holownia.
18 Polska 2050 lawmakers formed a separate parliamentary group (Centrum), splitting the coalition partner.
The United States and Israel launched airstrikes on Iran, starting the 2026 Iran war; Iran later closed the Strait of Hormuz.
President Nawrocki vetoed the law implementing the EU SAFE defence loan programme.
President Nawrocki signed the Energy Law amendment (UC84) on electricity market rules, fixed-price contracts and grid connections.
US-Iran ceasefire announced late on 7 April (US time), taking effect 8 April.
US-Iran talks in Islamabad failed and the US imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports.
Sejm rejected a no-confidence motion against Climate and Environment Minister Paulina Hennig-Kloska (238 to 213).
Poland signed a SAFE defence loan agreement with the EU despite the presidential veto of the implementing law.
US forces resumed strikes on Iran; Iran said it had closed the Strait of Hormuz.
A new 60-day US-Iran ceasefire was agreed.
President Nawrocki signed the law streamlining CHF-loan court cases, including automatic suspension of loan payments during litigation.
A Russian cruise missile entered Polish airspace and likely crashed in eastern Poland during an attack on Ukraine.
President Nawrocki vetoed an Energy Law amendment on grid-connection transition rules and an environmental protection law amendment.
Government adopted the 2027 budget draft with a 281.2 billion PLN deficit, a new 24% PIT bracket and electricity-cost subsidies for energy-intensive industry.

President Nawrocki vetoed three laws (Electoral Code seat redistribution, political advertising, implementing ECHR judgments) and signed eight, incl. the biogas/biomethane RES law and an energy-market settlement stability law (time = article publication).

Trump signed an executive order late Friday (US time) waiving the 100% tariffs on the largest buyers of Russian oil and gas and the 500% tariffs on Russian goods under the Graham sanctions law, days before they were due to take effect.

Sejm rejected the PiS no-confidence motion against Finance and Economy Minister Andrzej Domanski (204 for, 234 against, 231 needed); PM Tusk said he will ask the President to appoint Domanski deputy prime minister (time unknown; reports from 19:06).

Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia: debris from an intercepted drone set a fire near the Shaybah oilfield processing plant (2 killed; operations unaffected), and hours later Dammam's King Fahd airport was hit (1 killed). Brent rose about 4% on 22 Oct to a five-month high (~USD 113) (time unknown).

Sejm passed the government tax bill but, against the government (220-214, Petru/Kowalski amendment), struck the CIT increase from 19% to 22% for companies with revenue above EUR50m; Deputy FinMin Neneman: PLN6.2bn less 2027 revenue, spending cuts needed; PIT reform (12/24/32%) and bracket indexation from 2028 kept; bill goes to the Senate (time unknown).
